findings.summary: git.context upstreamKey (worktreePath:headSha:branch:baseSha) omits branchCreatedAt, so a branch deleted and recreated at the same HEAD emits the same eventId as its first life; an idempotent store drops the second event and B24 never splits the reused branch into a new flight.
findings.evidence: c03.test.ts 'FINDING: branch reuse at the same HEAD collides on eventId' asserts the collision (flip the assertion once B02 adds branchCreatedAt to the key)

findings.summary: A plain branch rename without a user alias mapping splits one piece of work into two provisional flights, though branchCreatedAt is identical across the rename; B24 could treat equal (repo, branchCreatedAt) as continuity.

gaps: Branch reuse split depends on reflog timestamps (1s resolution); reuse within the same second is indistinguishable.
